title: Free AI for teachers: quizzes, worksheets and slides · {name}
description: Free AI for teachers, in a browser tab: this week’s quiz, a worksheet in Word, slides, flash cards, the term’s lesson plans. Nothing to install.
h1: Your quizzes, worksheets and slides, made from your lesson.
lede: Give {name} your lesson, a page of the textbook or a few words. You get this week’s quiz, a worksheet in Word, slides for the board, flash cards or the term’s lesson plans, in your language and at your pupils’ level.
try.ask: This week’s quiz for my class: ten questions on our lesson, three answers to choose from for each.
quiz.head: This week’s quiz
quiz.question: Which fraction is the largest?
quiz.why: Cut a cake into 2 equal parts and each part is bigger than if you cut it into 3 or 4.
out.title: What you get, ready for class.
out.why: Ask in your own words, with your lesson if you like. Read it, change what you want, then use it.
out.quiz.text: Ten questions from your lesson, three answers each, played on the board, then scored and explained.
out.quiz.ask: A quiz on fractions for my class of 9 and 10-year-olds: ten questions, three answers to choose from for each.
out.worksheet.text: Exercises at three levels and the answers on a page of their own, in a Word file to change and print.
out.worksheet.ask: A worksheet on adding fractions for 9 and 10-year-olds, at three levels, with the answers on a separate page, as a Word document.
out.slides.text: A deck to page through and show full screen, written in the answer, or a PowerPoint file if you ask for one.
out.slides.ask: Six slides to introduce the water cycle to 11-year-olds.
out.cards.text: What to remember on cards, reviewed over the days, in a file that Anki and Quizlet import.
out.cards.ask: Flash cards for this week’s twelve Spanish words, with an example sentence for each.
out.plans.text: A lesson a week until the holidays, each with its aims and what to assess, as a table or a spreadsheet.
out.plans.ask: Lesson plans for this term in maths for my class of 10-year-olds: a lesson a week until the holidays, with its aims and what to assess, as a spreadsheet.
out.more: And whatever else you’d ask a colleague for: a letter to parents, a text at two reading levels, a marking grid.
worries.title: What teachers ask first.
worries.why: Whether it’s free, where pupils’ data goes, and whether you may use it.
free.title: Is it free?
free.text: Yes. {name} is free and open source, with nothing to install. The AI that answers can be free too:
free.list: With no account at all, on a computer with 12 GB of memory and a recent graphics chip: the AI on the computer, downloaded once (3.1 GB).
On any other computer, with a free account at an AI provider: “{free}”.
Or with a plan you already pay for.
data.title: And my pupils’ data?
data.text: There is no {name} server. What {name} keeps, your lessons, your files and its answers, stays on your computer, encrypted.
data.list: With the AI on the computer, nothing leaves it, pupils’ names included, even offline.
With any other AI, what you send goes to its provider, under its terms: leave pupils’ names out.
Your school’s rules on pupils’ data apply here as anywhere.
allowed.title: Am I allowed to use it?
allowed.text: Your school and your ministry decide what you use with pupils. {name} doesn’t replace the assistant your state gives you: it works beside it.
allowed.list: In Germany, the Länder offer schools AIS.chat, called telli until May 2026.
In France, the State’s AI assistant is open to its staff, with a version for teachers due in 2026–27.
{name} is for what you hand out: a quiz to play, a worksheet in Word, a deck, made at school or at home.
allowed.source: Schulministerium NRW, 18 May 2026 · Académie de Bordeaux, 19 June 2026
hand.title: Then hand it on.
hand.why: What you make is yours to give: to the class, to the parents, to your school.
hand.class.title: The class
hand.class.text: Play the quiz on the board together, print the worksheet, or send a link: a page that opens in any browser.
hand.parents.title: The parents
hand.parents.text: At home, a parent can give their child a profile of their own, set by the parent for the child’s age. Helping a child learn rather than giving the answer is measured before it’s promised.
hand.head.title: Your head teacher
hand.head.text: An AI charter for your school, written in {name} from a template and handed back as a Word file.
limits.title: The catch, plainly.
limits.items: The AI on the computer needs 12 GB of memory and a recent graphics chip. On other computers, the AI answers from its provider, with an account.
The AI on the computer is smaller than the big ones online: slower, and wrong more often.
Any AI can be wrong. Read a quiz or a worksheet before the class sees it.
It isn’t school software: no class lists, no mark book, no pupil accounts.
A tutor for your pupils isn’t promised yet: we first measure how often an AI gives them the answer anyway.
It doesn’t replace your school’s tools, its rules, or you.
faq.title: Your questions.
faq.items: Is it really free for teachers?
Yes. {name} is free and open source, for everyone. The AI can be free too: on a capable computer with no account, elsewhere with a free account at a provider.
Both. Say the age or the year, and the quiz, the worksheet or the slides are written for it.
Yes, with exercises at each level and the answers on a separate page. Check the numbers before you print: it can be wrong.
Add it to your request: a PDF, a Word file or a photo of the textbook page. A quiz then asks only what your lesson says.
In yours, and in the one your pupils are learning: a quiz for a Spanish class asks in Spanish, at their level.
No. You play the quiz on the board or hand out the worksheet. At home, a profile of their own is their parents’ choice.
In a recent browser, with nothing to install. The AI on the computer needs a capable one; on the others, use a free account.
Can I share it with colleagues?
Send them the Word file, or a link to the quiz or the slides. They open it in any browser, with nothing to install.
end.title: Start with this week’s quiz.
end.steps: Choose the AI that answers, the first time.
Say the lesson and the level, then read the quiz.
end.note: Opens {name} in this tab and asks for the quiz. Nothing to install.
